source_artifacts.locator: payments-agent agent card (as consumed by the orchestrator)

capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor task carrying the chosen vendor's bank details

inputs.source: Employee purchase request submitted through an SSO-authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments received from external senders

instructions.note: "choose the best one" gives no defined selection criteria (price, vendor reliability, bank-detail match against a master record), leaving vendor selection open to being swayed by a persuasive or fraudulent quote.

The prompt asserts payments-agent will handle any remaining checks, but the runtime notes show payments-agent performs no independent verification and pays whatever bank details the task contains, so the asserted downstream safety check does not actually exist.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (budget/item)
controls.decay_rationale: The human decision itself does not decay with model capability, but it approves only budget and item before any quote or bank detail exists, so it never reviews the specific payment destination that is actually executed.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: pay only vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: A more capable model can be persuaded that a spoofed quote 'is' from the approved vendor by name while using substituted bank details; the instruction checks vendor identity only, not payment destination, and compliance depends entirely on the model's judgment.

controls.name: Verify payment bank details against a vendor master record (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the payment destination to a verified vendor master record, independent of quote content, removes the model's ability to be misled by attacker-supplied bank details regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Human approval of the specific vendor and bank details before payment (missing)
Propagate approval record to payments-agent and validate before paying (missing)
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at payments-agent, this ties payment execution to a specific approved vendor and amount rather than to mere possession of the orchestrator's bearer token.

controls.name: Sign and pin the payments-agent card and verify peer identity (missing)
Spend or rate limit on payment delegation (missing)

findings.title: TC1 variant: untrusted vendor quote supplies bank details used for an irreversible payment

attack_path.note: Untrusted external vendor email supplies the quote, including bank account details, with no verification against a vendor master record.
Orchestrator hands the chosen quote's bank details to payments-agent to pay, gated only by a vendor-name allowlist instruction.
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task on trust in the orchestrator's bearer token, without independently verifying the destination.

forecast.watch_signal: Model swapped or upgraded for the orchestrator (subject.model.swappable) without a new review, or red-team testing shows the vendor-allowlist instruction increasingly bypassed by quotes that merely claim to be from an approved vendor.

evidence.observation: "Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company" and "Use the bank details from the chosen quote" (prompt.md:3) together mean an external, unverified party supplies the payment destination.
"payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task" confirms no independent verification occurs before payment.

recommendations.action: Bind payment destination to a verified vendor master record rather than bank details supplied in the quote; require out-of-band verification for any new or changed bank account before it can be used.
Require a human to approve the raw payment action (specific vendor and bank account), reviewed individually, before payments-agent executes it.
Alert when a quote's bank details differ from the vendor's on-file bank details.

findings.title: TC7: authority laundering — approval context does not propagate to payments-agent, which pays on trust in the orchestrator's token

forecast.watch_signal: Additional payment-capable peer agents are added, or the orchestrator is given authority to approve its own purchase requests without the separate manager step.

evidence.observation: "The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent." shows approval scope and execution scope are disconnected, with no provenance link carried forward.
"payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token" shows payments-agent treats possession of the token as sufficient authorization for any payment amount or recipient.

recommendations.action: Propagate a tamper-evident reference to the specific approval, including the final vendor and bank details, to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to validate the task against it before paying.
Replace the shared bearer token with per-transaction, narrowly scoped authorization tied to a specific vendor, amount, and bank account.
Log and reconcile executed payments against their originating approval record; alert on any payment with no matching record.

findings.title: ASI07/ASI04: unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card permits impersonation or silent redefinition

forecast.watch_signal: New peer agents are connected without signed, pinned definitions and mutual identity verification.

evidence.observation: "The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned" means the orchestrator cannot detect a substituted endpoint or a silently changed skill definition for payments-agent.
authentication.schemes is ["bearer"] only, with no mention of mutual authentication or peer identity verification of payments-agent itself.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent card and skill definitions, and verify peer identity (mutual TLS or signed identity) before sending payment tasks.
Alert on any change to the payments-agent card or endpoint between deployments.

findings.title: ASI08: no spend or rate limit on payment delegation

forecast.watch_signal: Volume or value of purchase requests per period rises without a corresponding spend or rate cap being added.

evidence.observation: No spend cap, rate limit, or per-period payment ceiling is described anywhere in the instructions.
No mention of any limit on how many payment tasks payments-agent will accept or execute from the orchestrator.

recommendations.action: Add a hard spend cap and rate limit on cap.delegate_payment per period, enforced independently of the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not state whether the orchestrator's bearer token used against payments-agent is scoped, rotated, or could be replayed by another caller impersonating the orchestrator.
Artifacts do not describe whether vendor quote contents, including bank details, are logged, cached, or exposed to any party beyond payments-agent.
Artifacts do not describe payments-agent's logging, storage, or downstream sharing of task payloads that contain vendor bank details.
Artifacts do not describe what information, such as approved budget or vendor-list details, is disclosed to external vendors when soliciting quotes.
Artifacts do not describe rate limiting or volume handling for inbound vendor quote emails, so resilience to a flood of fake quotes cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe email authentication such as SPF, DKIM, or DMARC for inbound vendor quotes, so non-repudiation of the sender cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe encryption or access controls on the A2A payment task payload in transit beyond bearer-token authentication.
The vendor list is only read by the orchestrator through cap.vendor_list_read, a read-only action; no capability in this design writes to the list, so the agent cannot tamper with it.
Artifacts do not describe whether vendor list contents are ever included in outbound messages or otherwise exposed to external parties.
Reading a static approved vendor list is a bounded internal read with no external input influencing its volume or frequency of access.
Artifacts do not describe integrity protections, such as signing or write-once storage, for the manager approval record.
Artifacts do not describe access controls on the approval record beyond its use within the orchestrator itself.
The approval record is a single per-request record created by a human approval step and is not an attacker-reachable resource that could be flooded.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted vendor quote email can directly determine the bank destination of an irreversible payment (find.vendor_quote_bank_substitution). Residual drops to high only because of a single prompt instruction restricting payments to vendors on an approved list, which checks vendor name but not bank account authenticity. Three further gaps keep residual at high across the board: approval context (budget approval) never propagates to payments-agent and payments-agent accepts any task on the orchestrator's shared bearer token (find.authority_laundering_a2a); the payments-agent card is unsigned and unpinned, so its identity and definition cannot be trusted (find.unpinned_payments_agent_card); and there is no spend or rate limit on payment delegation (find.no_spend_rate_limit). Forecast returns to critical because the one credited control is a behavioral, model-dependent instruction that a model upgrade, longer task horizons, or increased autonomy would be expected to erode, while the structural fixes that would actually close these paths (bank-detail verification bound to a vendor master record, propagated approval context, signed/pinned peer identity, and a spend cap) are all currently absent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.
No captured A2A traffic, logs, or token configuration were provided; auth_method and credential_scope for the orchestrator-to-payments-agent call are inferred from the agent card and runtime notes.
Approval volume (requests per approver per day) for the manager approval step is not stated and is recorded as unknown.
No information on email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) for inbound vendor quotes was provided; spoofing feasibility is assumed plausible but not confirmed.
